steps.reasons: Literal title. The header it lights (SIX LINES // QUERY 22) is on the real screen from frame 0. 11 and 11 characters.

steps.text:
SIX LINES, L1
AT THE BOTTOM.
steps.reasons: True of both the plot (lineZ puts index 0 lowest) and the log (rows printed [5..0] top to bottom, so L1 is the last row). Lights show the order. 13 and 14 characters.

steps.text:
SOLID LINE: YANG.
BROKEN LINE: YIN.
steps.reasons: Needed for every later step. 22 gives a solid L1 and a broken L2 side by side, and the log prints YANG and YIN on those rows. 17 and 17 characters.

steps.text:
ODD PLACES WANT
YANG, EVEN YIN.
steps.reasons: Matches place() in Readout.tsx. The Tuan and Xiang use it (當位 / 位不當), and Wang Bi's Lüeli (辯位) states it for 2-5, which the caption covers. His own note on 22 line 1 says 居於无位 ('holds no place'), which confirms the caption's caveat. The lights have two sweeps (L1 L3 L5, then L2 L4 L6), and 3.6 s is tight for both plus two lines of text. Give it about 4 s (see notes).

steps.text:
RIGHT KIND: IN.
WRONG KIND: OUT.
steps.reasons: Literal. The example is well chosen: L2 and L5 are both YIN, one IN and one OUT, so the viewer sees that the place decides it, not the line. It also sets up the last step (L5 is OUT and still the master). Wang Bi's notes on 22 use the same terms: line 2 得其位, line 3 居得其位.

The + fixes round 2's clash with the 4-6 ranges. It matches `answering` (bracket only where lines[i] != lines[i+3]), and for 22 that is only 1+4. Wang Bi's note on 22 line 4 says 有應在初 ('it has a match in line 1'), and his note on line 2 says 无應 ('no match'). Both agree with the lights. 18 and 18 characters, at the limit. The lights (a bracket, then two pairs with no bracket) are the most for any step, so this step also needs about 4 s.

Uses the screen's own words, UPPER and LOWER, in the same top-to-bottom order as the screen. 18 and 18 characters. The trigram rows also show MOUNTAIN · STILL and FIRE · CLINGING (Shuo Gua 7), with 艮 and 離 beside them. The script does not explain those, and that is fine: the English is already next to the Chinese, and the words explain themselves.

Matches the code (· CENTRE on index 1 and 4) and the Tuan's 得中. Wang Bi's note on 22's Tuan says line 2 居位得中 ('holds its place and gains the centre'). The lights go from the brackets to the two middle lines, which is the right order. With the centre-makes-up-for-OUT step gone, the viewer just sees L5's row, which reads YIN OUT · CENTRE, and that is enough.

steps.text:
◄ MARKS THE LINES
TO LOOK AT.
steps.reasons: The text is accurate across the 35 shorts (mark[] puts ◄ and amber on those rows and plot lines). The lights are not: they include 'the finding' (> THE SOFT COMES TO ADORN THE STRONG.), but the text never mentions it. A newcomer will read the lit finding as part of what ◄ means, or not know what it is. On 22's real screen the finding is DIM, not amber, because there is a master. Either drop it from the lights (the simpler fix) or give it its own step, which costs time. Also keep the real screen's blink on the marked lines (opacity 0.35 every 6 frames), since that is what viewers will see in the shorts.

rewrite.text:
◄ MARKS THE LINES
TO LOOK AT.
rewrite.lights: L2 and L5 in their real amber, blinking as in the shorts, with ◄ on their log rows; the finding stays dimmed

steps.text:
WANG BI NAMES THE
LINE THAT RULES.
steps.reasons: The source and the claim are right. The Wang Bi note on 賁 six-five is 處得尊位，為飾之主 ('holding the honoured place, it is the master of adornment'), and 主 is his idea (Lüeli, 明彖). The script does not say he chose L5 because of the centre or despite OUT, and that restraint is correct, because he gives neither reason. The lights (the WANG BI line and L5) are the only thing that tells the viewer which of the two ◄ lines is named. This last step also has to leave time to read the Chinese line and its English line under it, so give it the longest hold.

caption.rewrite: How to read the green screen in 35 of our shorts, using 22 Grace. The in/out rule comes from the Ten Wings; Wang Bi (AD 226–249) applied it only to lines 2 to 5.

look.notes: Round 2's amber problem is fixed: the explained part goes to full green, the rest dims, and amber is used only where the real screen uses it. Four things are still open. (1) Placement: 'above the header' is the 0-150 px band, which is under Instagram's top overlay (Meta's Reels safe zone leaves about the top 14%, about 270 px, clear). Check it on a phone before rendering. If it is covered, put the step text in the prompt area (y 1360 and below) for steps 1-8, where the WANG BI and finding lines are dimmed anyway, and move it above the header only for the last two steps. Or drop the header band for this short and use its 90 px for the text. (2) The step text needs a look that can't be mistaken for part of the readout, or it will compete with the lit parts: the same pixel font in plain white, no glow. Say so in 'look'. (3) 'Without the lesson line' is right. Say also that the > finding line is shown, dimmed, as on the real 22 screen, so the step-9 lights fix above is possible. (4) Say that the plot keeps its slow turn and the marked lines keep their blink, so the explainer looks like the shorts it explains. 'Fully built from the start' is the right call: it avoids re-timing the acts, which are shares of the duration.

notes: Round 3 adopts round 2's rewrites correctly: pairs are written with + and ranges with a dash, UPPER/LOWER are the screen's words, the centre-makes-up step is cut, and amber is kept for the last two steps. Every claim is credited to the right source, and Wang Bi's own notes on 22 back each term on screen: 居於无位 (line 1 has no place), 得其位 (lines 2 and 3), 有應在初 (4 matches 1), 居位得中 (2 is a centre), 為飾之主 (5 is master). The finding line is the Tuan's 柔來而文剛, which Wang Bi reads as line 2, so marking L2 is justified. The remaining fixes are small: (1) Step 9's lights include the finding, but the text doesn't mention it. (2) The caption's 'judge each line' overstates the Ten Wings, since the Xiang on 22 line 5 (六五之吉，有喜也) says nothing about place, so the rewrite says the rule comes from them. (3) Pacing: even 3.6 s steps short the two steps that have two light sweeps and the last step, which has the most to read, and give too much time to the title. Suggested times: 0.0, 2.8, 6.0, 9.2 (4.2 s), 13.4, 16.8 (4.2 s), 21.0, 24.4, 27.8, 31.2 to the end (about 5 s). That is still 10 steps in about 36 s. A newcomer can follow it in one viewing if they already know what a hexagram is. It is a pinned reference and will be rewatched, so the density is acceptable. (4) An option for the user, not a fix: the header reads QUERY 22 on all 35 shorts, and 'query' can suggest asking a question of the book, which this series does not do. Changing it to, say, HEXAGRAM 22 would mean re-rendering every short, so only offer it. Copy check: all 20 lines are at most 18 characters (four are exactly 18: 1+4, 2+5, 3+6 LINK / IF YIN MEETS YANG. / UPPER TRIGRAM: 4-6 / LOWER TRIGRAM: 1-3), uppercase, and free of the banned words. Round 2's optional prop change (22 master.en as 'Line five, master of Adornment', as in 10, 13 and 16) is still open. It would make the screen itself say which ◄ line Wang Bi names.
